Article (plain text of the PDF):

Sign change of the square-hexagonal difference of the three-body
lattice energy Tν at νc ≈ 3.92 in two dimensions
Verifier-Gated Discovery Lab
Preprint, October 4, 2026

Abstract
We study the three-body energy Tν (L) of two-dimensional Bravais lattices L of unit
covolume, a sum of (|x||y||x − y|)−ν over ordered pairs of distinct nonzero lattice vectors.
The question is whether f (ν) = Tν (square) − Tν (hexagonal) changes sign, which would signal
a hexagonal-to-square transition, and whether the sign change lies in an interval of width at
most 0.05. A targeted search of 45 abstracts did not find this statement in the literature.
Numerically, f (3.9) = 5.300e-03 and f (3.94) = -6.238e-03, so f changes sign between
ν = 3.9 and ν = 3.94. The energies are computed by cube summation with Richardson
extrapolation in the cutoff. The main limitation is that the result is a numerical observation
with an error estimate. It carries no rigorous certificate, and the location of νc inside the
interval is not established.
Keywords: three-body lattice energy, Bravais lattices, hexagonal lattice, square lattice,
phase transition, Richardson extrapolation

1

Introduction

The three-body energy Tν assigns to each Bravais lattice of unit covolume a sum over triangles
with a vertex at the origin. For two-dimensional lattices, a natural question is which lattice
minimizes Tν and how this depends on the exponent ν. The square and hexagonal lattices are
the two obvious candidates. If the preferred lattice among them switches as ν varies, there is a
critical exponent νc at which f (ν) = Tν (square) − Tν (hexagonal) vanishes.
No literature claim is available to us here. In a targeted search of 45 abstracts on 2026-10-04
we did not find the statement below. This is a statement about the search only and not a claim
of priority.
We report a numerical observation that f changes sign between ν = 3.9 and ν = 3.94. This
places a critical exponent in an interval of width at most 0.05. The evidence is two evaluations
with an error estimate. We do not prove the sign change.
Summary of results.
• Observation 1 shows that f is positive at ν = 3.9 and negative at ν = 3.94, so f changes
sign between these two exponents.
• Together with continuity of f in ν, assumed and not proved here, this localizes νc to an
interval of width at most 0.05 (Observation 1).
• All results are numerical and carry no rigorous certificate (Method, Discussion).

Lattices are normalized to covolume 1. A lattice is parametrized by τ = x + iy in the fundamental
domain. The square lattice and the hexagonal lattice are the two points of this domain compared
below. We write
f (ν) = Tν (square) − Tν (hexagonal).
Fixed model parameters:
• covolume = 1 for all Bravais lattices;
• cutoff R ∈ {32, 48, 64, 96}, with the summation cube [−R, R]d in lattice coordinates and
Richardson extrapolation in R;
• νdirect = 12: for ν ≥ 12, direct summation replaces FFT convolution.
Assumption (A): f is continuous in ν on the interval considered. It is used only to pass from
a sign change of two sampled values to a zero. It is not checked here.

3

Method

The sign change is established numerically. The two values of f are obtained from cube summation,
combined by Richardson extrapolation in R, and accompanied by an error estimate. The sign of
f at each of the two sample points is then compared with the size of the error estimate.
We separate three classes of statements.
• Proved statements: none.
• Computer-assisted rigorous statements: none. No exact rational arithmetic, symbolic
positivity proof or interval enclosure underlies the main observation.
• Numerical observations: the sign of f at ν = 3.9 and ν = 3.94, and the resulting sign-change
interval.
The trusted base is the floating-point summation code and the extrapolation in R. A third
party can re-run the computation with the commands in the Declarations. Anything beyond
the two stated values, in particular the precise location of νc , counts at most as a numerical
candidate.
The results were produced and checked by an automated, verifier-gated laboratory. The
statement above was accepted only after the verifier had recomputed the values.

4

Results

Numerical observation 1 (Sign change of f between ν = 3.9 and ν = 3.94). In two dimensions,
the difference f (ν) = Tν (square) − Tν (hexagonal) changes sign between ν = 3.9 and ν = 3.94
(numerically, with error estimate). The verifier values are f (3.9) = 5.300e-03 and f (3.94) =
-6.238e-03. Under Assumption (A), a zero of f , that is a critical exponent νc , lies in an interval
of width at most 0.05.

Negative results

This article records no negative result of its own. Adversarial counter-checks of the main
observation are reported in Appendix A.

6

Discussion, limitations and open questions

The observation shows that Tν (square) − Tν (hexagonal) is positive at ν = 3.9 and negative at
ν = 3.94. It does not show which lattice is the global minimizer at other exponents. Only the
two lattices in the difference were compared. The sign change is numerical, and the zero between
the sample points is inferred under Assumption (A).
Open questions:
•

(i) Can the location of the sign change between ν = 3.9 and ν = 3.94 be narrowed by
evaluating f at further exponents?
• (ii) Can the sign of f at the two sample points be certified with interval arithmetic, so
that the sign change becomes computer-assisted rigorous?
• (iii) Which lattice minimizes Tν over the whole fundamental domain on either side of the
sign change?

3

 Novelty search: queries were “three-body energy hexagonal square lattice”, “three-body
Bravais lattice sign change”, “lattice energy comparison nu parameter” and “hexagonal quadratic
lattice potential difference”, covering 45 abstracts.
Red-team statistics: 2 counter-checks in total, with 0 passed, 2 did not pass and 0 not
executable.
• Counter-check 1 (opposite statement): if the hexagonal-to-square transition were false, the
hexagonal lattice would remain the global minimum at large ν. The tested answer asserts
that the square lattice is the minimum at ν = 8. Result: did not pass. The verifier ran
a search on an 18er grid with 6 polishings at the cutoffs 48 and 64 and found the square
lattice.
• Counter-check 2 (edge case): if the true sign change were near ν ≈ 5 rather than near
3.918, the claimed value would be wrong. Result: did not pass. The verifier values are
f (5.0) = -2.919e-01 and f (5.05) = -3.039e-01.
An unverified interpretation proposed a sign change at νc ≈ 3.91837, positive at smaller and
negative at larger ν. It has status hypothesis, open, and is not used as a result in this article.
